HIV 101

What is HIV?

HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system. Without treatment, HIV can progress to its most advanced stage, called AIDS.

HIV and AIDS are not the same. HIV is the virus; AIDS is an advanced stage that may develop when HIV is untreated. With effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), HIV can be managed as a chronic health condition and people living with HIV can live long, healthy lives.

A term you may see: ART is antiretroviral therapy, treatment that stops HIV from replicating in the body.

Transmission

HIV is not transmitted through everyday togetherness.

HIV can be transmitted through certain body fluids, including blood, semen, vaginal fluids, and breast milk. It can also be transmitted during pregnancy or delivery.

HIV is not transmitted through hugging, shaking hands, sharing food or water, or ordinary social contact.

A common misunderstanding

Appearance cannot tell you whether someone is living with HIV. Only an HIV test can determine HIV status.

Testing & Prevention

Starting points for informed decisions.

HIV testing can connect people with prevention, treatment, and support. A reactive result from one test needs confirmation under the national testing algorithm.

HIV testing

Timing and window periods depend on the test and time since possible exposure. A trained provider can explain when testing or retesting is appropriate.

PrEP

PrEP is antiretroviral medicine used by people without HIV to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Access should follow current Indonesian services and guidance.

PEP

PEP is antiretroviral medicine used after a possible exposure. Because timing matters, contact a health service promptly after a recent possible exposure.

Treatment

ART, viral load, and CD4.

ART stops HIV from replicating and reduces the amount of virus in the body. It does not cure HIV, but it helps the immune system become stronger.

Viral load is the amount of HIV in the blood. Effective treatment can reduce it until standard tests cannot detect it.

CD4 is a type of immune cell used as one part of assessing the health of a person living with HIV. Results should be interpreted with a health professional.

U=U

Undetectable = Untransmittable

Undetectable means no sexual transmission.

When a person takes ART and maintains an undetectable viral load, they do not sexually transmit HIV. Starting and staying on treatment supports health and prevention.

U=U specifically concerns sexual transmission. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, shared injecting equipment, or treatment interruption require separate clinical guidance.
